title: DR1 labels the dashboard's primary action "Create a new notification"; the frontend labels it "Start a new notification".

finding.frontend: The button under the introductory paragraph reads "Start a new notification" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:7, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:30-33).
finding.prototype: DR1 labels the same action "Create a new notification" (app/views/dashboard.html:33-37), and uses that wording again as a link at the foot of its submission confirmation page, so it is the service's settled name for the action.
finding.difference: Change the button text to "Create a new notification". This finding is about the wording only — whether the control is a GOV.UK start button or a plain button is a chrome question and is not being asked here.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the frontend dashboard's primary button reading "Create a new notification".
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (fe-dashboard-populated.html:109-114 renders "Start a new notification"; dr1-dashboard.html:241-243 renders "Create a new notification") and the fe-dashboard-populated and dr1-dashboard-filters-open screenshots; opened dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:7 and app/views/dashboard.html:34; ran the falsifier by grepping both frontend dashboard captures for "Create a new notification" — no match, so it does not fire. Checked the second-use claim: app/views/notification-submitted.html:57 carries the same wording as a link. Both named controls resolve to real text on the screens listed, so both crop. CORRECT.
